import sys
from collections import Counter

input = sys.stdin.read
data = input().split()

n = int(data[0])
s = data[1]
beauty = list(map(int, data[2:n+2]))

# Create a list of tuples (beauty, character), sorted by beauty descending
beauty_char_pairs = sorted(zip(beauty, s), reverse=True)

# Find how many of each character we have
char_count = Counter(s)

# Initialize the antipalindromic string t and its used beauty
t = [''] * n
used_beauty = 0

# Fill the first half of the antipalindromic string t
for i in range(n // 2):
    for index, (b, char) in enumerate(beauty_char_pairs):
        if char_count[char] > 0:
            # Place the character and decrease its count
            t[i] = char
            char_count[char] -= 1
            used_beauty += b
            # Mark the beauty-char pair as used by setting beauty to -1
            beauty_char_pairs[index] = (-1, char)
            break

# Fill the second half of the antipalindromic string t
for i in range(n // 2, n):
    for index, (b, char) in enumerate(beauty_char_pairs):
        # Check if the character is different from the mirrored position
        if char_count[char] > 0 and char != t[n - i - 1]:
            # Place the character and decrease its count
            t[i] = char
            char_count[char] -= 1
            used_beauty += b
            # Mark the beauty-char pair as used by setting beauty to -1
            beauty_char_pairs[index] = (-1, char)
            break

print(used_beauty)
T_solution:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.read
data = input().split()

n = int(data[0])
s = data[1]
b = list(map(int, data[2:]))

freq = [0] * 26
for char in s:
    freq[ord(char) - ord('a')] += 1

result = sum(max(b[i], b[n - i - 1]) for i in range(n // 2))
print(result)

8
